**UPSA ASSEMBLY PLATFORM**  
**Backend Schema**  
PostgreSQL schema for the UPSA Assembly Platform: 106 tables in 8 domain schemas, with the rules, security and functions that keep stock, cost and traceability trustworthy.

1\. Purpose and how to use this document
========================================

This is the data contract for UAP. It is delivered as this reference plus an executable SQL file (UAP\_05\_Backend\_Schema.sql) generated from the same catalogue, so the two cannot drift. The SQL targets PostgreSQL 16 on Supabase; migrations in the repository are split from it as described in section 12.

| **Item** | **Detail** |
| --- | --- |
| Schemas | core, catalog, proc, inv, prod, sales, fin, svc (8) |
| Tables | 106 |
| Columns | 1300 |
| Append-only tables | 6 (ledger, audit, timelines, snapshots, cost history) |
| Audited tables | 31 with automatic before/after capture |
| Views | 7 (stock on hand and available, buildable quantity, PO line status, open receivables, budget versus actual, unit cost check) |
| Domain functions | Landed-cost run and post, unit finalisation, genealogy forward and reverse, access-token hook, document numbering |

<table><tbody><tr><td><strong>Validation status</strong><br>The SQL was parsed and loaded on a real PostgreSQL instance and exercised for: append-only ledger rejection, journal balance enforcement, closed-period lock, document numbering, the access-token hook, and a landed-cost allocation whose results matched the worked example in the TDD (freight 480,000 and 360,000 on value; clearing 100,000 and 50,000 on quantity; both sum exactly to the charge). The test instance used stubs for Supabase auth and omitted the citext, pg_trgm and unaccent extensions, so those parts must be verified on a Supabase project. Remaining logic (RLS behaviour with real JWTs, reservations, the full production path) is covered by the pgTAP plan in section 13.</td></tr></tbody></table>

2\. Conventions
===============

| **Topic** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| Identifiers | uuid primary keys named id with gen\_random\_uuid(); bigint identity only for high-volume append tables (ledger, audit, outbox). profiles.id equals the Supabase auth user id. |
| Naming | snake\_case; tables plural; foreign keys <entity>\_id; money columns end in \_minor; document numbers end in \_no; timestamps end in \_at, dates in \_on. |
| Money | bigint minor units (pesewas for GHS) next to a currency column. amount\_base\_minor is the GHS value at the rate stored on the row. Never float. |
| Quantities | numeric(16,4) so fractional units (cables by metre, consumables) are possible; serial-tracked items are always whole units. |
| Time | timestamptz stored in UTC; business dates as date. Document numbering year uses Africa/Accra. |
| Status fields | text with a CHECK (status IN (…)) rather than enum types, so values can change in a forward migration without type rewrites. Allowed values appear in the table reference. |
| Standard columns | Mutable tables carry id, created\_at, updated\_at, version (incremented by trigger for optimistic concurrency). Append-only tables carry id and created\_at only. |
| Document numbers | Series such as PO-2026-000123, assigned by core.next\_doc\_no(series) through a row-locked counter in core.doc\_sequences; gap-free within a committed transaction. Series per table: SUP (suppliers), ACC (customer\_accounts), REQ (requisitions), PO (purchase\_orders), SHP (shipments), GRN (goods\_receipts), LC (landed\_cost\_runs), RMA (supplier\_rmas), TRF (transfers), ADJ (adjustments), CNT (stock\_counts), AO (assembly\_orders), MI (material\_issues), B (units), QC (qc\_inspections), RW (rework\_orders), ORD (internal\_orders), DSP (dispatches), RET (sales\_returns), INV (invoices), PAY (payments), EXP (expenses), TKT (service\_tickets), JE (journal\_entries). |
| Append-only | A trigger raises APPEND\_ONLY for UPDATE or DELETE on the ledger, audit log, cost history, snapshots and timelines. Corrections are new rows. |
| Audit | core.audit\_trigger() writes before and after images to core.audit\_log for 31 business tables, stripping encrypted columns. The API sets app.actor\_id and app.request\_id per transaction. |
| Soft references | Cross-schema references are real foreign keys, added after table creation so creation order never matters. Only core.audit\_log has no foreign keys by design (it must outlive its subjects). |
| Deletion | Business records are not deleted; they change status. Line tables cascade from their header while the header is in draft. |
| Extensions | pgcrypto, citext, pg\_trgm, unaccent; vector is reserved for the Phase 3 repair knowledge base and not created yet. |
| Encryption | Supplier bank details, bank accounts, licence keys and API secrets are stored encrypted (application-level, key outside the database) and are excluded from browser-role grants. |

3\. Domain map
==============

Simplified entity map of the principal tables and relationships; dashed lines are optional or weaker links. The full relationships are in the table reference.  
![Entity relationship overview](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 1 — Principal entities by domain schema_

| **Spine** | **How the domains connect** |
| --- | --- |
| Imports to stock | shipments → goods\_receipts → goods\_receipt\_lines → lots / component\_serials → stock\_ledger; shipment\_charges → landed\_cost\_allocations → lot and unit cost |
| Stock to units | material\_issue\_lines move parts to WIP; unit\_components records exactly which serial and lot sits in which unit |
| Units to customers | units → order\_line\_units → dispatches → warranties; invoices and payments follow the order |
| After-sales | service\_tickets consume service\_parts, update unit\_components, and can open supplier\_rmas |
| Money | Business events post journal\_entries / journal\_lines through the outbox; fiscal\_periods lock history |

5\. Table reference
===================

_Each table lists its columns beyond the standard ones. Constraints: PK primary key, NN not null, UQ unique, FK foreign key. Allowed values for text status fields are shown in Notes._

Identity, reference data, approvals, audit, platform.

### core.profiles

One row per staff user; id equals the Supabase auth user id. Only the Super Admin has is\_admin. Standard: created\_at, updated\_at, version.

| **Column** | **Type** | **Constraints** | **Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | uuid | PK · FK → auth.users | auth.users.id |
| full\_name | text | NN |  |

| phone | text |  |  |
| staff\_no | text | UQ |  |
| job\_title | text |  |  |
| department | text |  |  |

6\. Integrity rules enforced by the database
============================================

| **Rule** | **Mechanism** | **Where** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock and cost history cannot be edited | Trigger core.reject\_mutation() | inv.stock\_ledger, inv.item\_cost\_history, inv.stock\_snapshots, core.audit\_log, timelines |
| A serial unit is reserved at most once | Partial unique index on active reservations | inv.reservations |
| Only one active BOM per item | Partial unique index | catalog.boms |
| Accepted + rejected = received | CHECK | proc.goods\_receipt\_lines |
| Inspector must not have built or worked on the unit | Trigger prod.assert\_inspector\_independent() | prod.qc\_inspections |
| Requester cannot decide own approval | CHECK decided\_by <> requested\_by | core.approvals |
| Journal entries balance | Deferred constraint trigger | fin.journal\_lines |
| Closed periods are read-only; entry date inside period | Trigger fin.assert\_period\_open() | fin.journal\_entries |
| One journal entry per source document and event | Unique (source\_type, source\_id, source\_event) | fin.journal\_entries |
| Unit cannot be finalised without passed tests and QC | Function prod.finalise\_unit() raises TESTS\_INCOMPLETE, QC\_NOT\_PASSED | prod |
| Landed cost allocations sum exactly to each charge | Largest-remainder rounding in proc.run\_landed\_cost() | proc |
| One warranty per unit | Unique unit\_id | svc.warranties |
| Payment allocates to exactly one invoice type | CHECK | fin.payment\_allocations |
| Defect belongs to exactly one inspection type | CHECK | prod.qc\_defects |
| Document numbers unique and gap-free | Row-locked counter plus unique columns | core.next\_doc\_no |
| Supplier invoice numbers unique per supplier | Unique (supplier\_id, invoice\_no) | proc.supplier\_invoices |
| Exchange rate unique per currency, date and source | Unique constraint | core.exchange\_rates |

Rules the database cannot express alone (aggregate PO limits per supplier, dual control on supplier bank changes, credit-limit checks) are enforced in API modules and re-checked by functions where they post money or stock.

7\. Functions, triggers and views
=================================

| **Object** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- |
| core.next\_doc\_no(series) / core.set\_doc\_no() | Gap-free document numbers; trigger fills \*\_no columns on insert |
| core.touch\_updated() | Maintains updated\_at and version |
| core.audit\_trigger() | Before and after images into the audit log; strips encrypted columns |
| core.has\_scope(), has\_any\_scope(), is\_staff(), is\_admin() | JWT-claim helpers for RLS |
| core.access\_token\_hook(event) | Builds scopes, roles, is\_admin, staff\_status claims from role templates plus extra minus revoked scopes; suspended users get no scopes |
| core.ensure\_month\_partition() | Creates monthly partitions for the audit log and stock ledger (scheduled with pg\_cron) |
| proc.run\_landed\_cost(shipment) | Allocates each non-recoverable charge by its basis across accepted receipt lines, largest-remainder rounding |
| proc.post\_landed\_cost(run, user) | Updates unit and lot cost, appends cost history, queues postings; reversal is a new run with approval |
| prod.finalise\_unit(unit, inspection, user) | Verifies tests and QC, assigns the final serial, snapshots material and labour cost, writes the finished-goods ledger row |
| prod.unit\_genealogy(serial) / inv.units\_by\_lot(lot) | Forward and reverse traceability |
| inv.v\_stock\_on\_hand, inv.v\_stock\_available | Snapshot plus ledger since; minus active reservations |
| prod.v\_buildable | How many units of each model can be built from warehouse stock now |
| proc.v\_po\_line\_status | Ordered versus received per PO line (derived, not stored) |
| fin.v\_ar\_open, fin.v\_budget\_vs\_actual | Open receivables with days overdue; budget versus actual by cost centre |
| prod.v\_unit\_cost | Control view comparing live component cost with the frozen unit cost |

7.1 Planned functions (specified, implemented in Phase 1 migrations)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

| **Function** | **Contract** |
| --- | --- |
| inv.post\_goods\_receipt(grn, user) | Writes ledger rows, lots and serials for accepted lines, quarantine rows for rejects, updates PO status; idempotent per GRN |
| inv.reserve\_units(order\_line, n) | Locks candidate units with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, inserts reservations; raises UNIT\_UNAVAILABLE |
| prod.release\_assembly\_order(ao) | Snapshots materials, creates unit rows, reserves parts |
| prod.issue\_materials(issue) | Moves parts to WIP, marks serials issued, writes ledger rows |
| sales.dispatch\_order(dispatch, user) | Locks units, writes dispatch ledger rows, status changes, queues invoice and cost-of-sales postings |
| sales.confirm\_handover(dispatch, ...) | Records recipient and signature; creates the warranty from the unit serial |
| svc.consume\_part(ticket, ...) | Issues a part, replaces a unit\_components row (new row linked via replaced\_by\_id), optionally opens an RMA |
| fin.post\_event(topic, payload) | Turns outbox events into journal entries using the posting table in the TDD |

7.2 SQL excerpts
----------------

### Access-token hook

create or replace function core.access\_token\_hook(event jsonb) returns jsonb language plpgsql stable security definer set search\_path = '' as $$  
declare v\_uid uuid := (event ->> 'user\_id')::uuid; v\_claims jsonb := event -> 'claims';  
v\_scopes text\[\]; v\_roles text\[\]; v\_admin boolean; v\_status text;  
begin  
select p.is\_admin, p.status into v\_admin, v\_status from core.profiles p where p.id = v\_uid;  
select coalesce(array\_agg(distinct s), '{}') into v\_scopes from (  
select unnest(r.default\_scopes) as s from core.user\_roles ur join core.roles r on r.id = ur.role\_id where ur.user\_id = v\_uid  
union select unnest(p.extra\_scopes) from core.profiles p where p.id = v\_uid) x  
where s <> all (select unnest(p2.revoked\_scopes) from core.profiles p2 where p2.id = v\_uid);  
select coalesce(array\_agg(r.code), '{}') into v\_roles from core.user\_roles ur join core.roles r on r.id = ur.role\_id where ur.user\_id = v\_uid;  
if coalesce(v\_status, 'suspended') <> 'active' then v\_scopes := '{}'; end if;  
v\_claims := v\_claims || jsonb\_build\_object('scopes', to\_jsonb(v\_scopes), 'roles', to\_jsonb(v\_roles),  
'is\_admin', coalesce(v\_admin, false), 'staff\_status', coalesce(v\_status, 'none'));  
return jsonb\_set(event, '{claims}', v\_claims);  
end $$;  
grant usage on schema core to supabase\_auth\_admin;  
grant execute on function core.access\_token\_hook to supabase\_auth\_admin;  
revoke execute on function core.access\_token\_hook from authenticated, anon, public;  
grant select on core.profiles, core.user\_roles, core.roles to supabase\_auth\_admin;

### Landed-cost allocation

create or replace function proc.run\_landed\_cost(p\_shipment uuid) returns uuid language plpgsql security definer set search\_path = '' as $$  
declare v\_run uuid; ch record; v\_total numeric; v\_rem bigint;  
begin  
insert into proc.landed\_cost\_runs(shipment\_id, status) values (p\_shipment, 'draft') returning id into v\_run;  
create temporary table \_lc on commit drop as  
select l.id as grn\_line\_id, coalesce(l.goods\_value\_base\_minor, 0)::numeric as val,  
coalesce(sl.weight\_kg, 0) \* l.qty\_accepted / nullif(l.qty\_received, 0) as wt,  
coalesce(sl.volume\_cbm, 0) \* l.qty\_accepted / nullif(l.qty\_received, 0) as vol,  
l.qty\_accepted as q  
from proc.goods\_receipt\_lines l  
join proc.goods\_receipts g on g.id = l.grn\_id  
left join proc.shipment\_lines sl on sl.id = l.shipment\_line\_id  
where g.shipment\_id = p\_shipment and g.status = 'posted' and l.qty\_accepted > 0;  
if not exists (select 1 from \_lc) then raise exception 'NO\_ACCEPTED\_LINES' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
for ch in select \* from proc.shipment\_charges where shipment\_id = p\_shipment and not is\_recoverable and allocation\_basis <> 'manual' loop  
select sum(case ch.allocation\_basis when 'value' then val when 'weight' then wt when 'volume' then vol else q end) into v\_total from \_lc;  
if coalesce(v\_total, 0) = 0 then raise exception 'NO\_BASIS\_FOR\_CHARGE %', ch.id using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
insert into proc.landed\_cost\_allocations(run\_id, grn\_line\_id, charge\_id, basis, basis\_value, share\_pct, amount\_minor)  
select v\_run, x.grn\_line\_id, ch.id, ch.allocation\_basis, x.b, x.b / v\_total \* 100, floor(ch.amount\_base\_minor \* x.b / v\_total)::bigint  
from (select grn\_line\_id, case ch.allocation\_basis when 'value' then val when 'weight' then wt when 'volume' then vol else q end as b from \_lc) x;  
select ch.amount\_base\_minor - sum(a.amount\_minor) into v\_rem from proc.landed\_cost\_allocations a where a.run\_id = v\_run and a.charge\_id = ch.id;  
update proc.landed\_cost\_allocations set amount\_minor = amount\_minor + 1  
where id in (select a.id from proc.landed\_cost\_allocations a where a.run\_id = v\_run and a.charge\_id = ch.id  
order by (ch.amount\_base\_minor \* a.basis\_value / v\_total) - floor(ch.amount\_base\_minor \* a.basis\_value / v\_total) desc, a.id  
limit v\_rem);  
end loop;  
return v\_run;  
end $$;

### Landed-cost posting

create or replace function proc.post\_landed\_cost(p\_run uuid, p\_user uuid) returns void language plpgsql security definer set search\_path = '' as $$  
declare r record;  
begin  
if not exists (select 1 from proc.landed\_cost\_runs where id = p\_run and status = 'draft') then raise exception 'RUN\_NOT\_DRAFT' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
for r in select a.grn\_line\_id, sum(a.amount\_minor) as added, l.item\_id, l.qty\_accepted, coalesce(l.goods\_value\_base\_minor, 0) as goods  
from proc.landed\_cost\_allocations a join proc.goods\_receipt\_lines l on l.id = a.grn\_line\_id  
where a.run\_id = p\_run group by a.grn\_line\_id, l.item\_id, l.qty\_accepted, l.goods\_value\_base\_minor loop  
update proc.goods\_receipt\_lines set landed\_unit\_cost\_minor = round((r.goods + r.added)::numeric / nullif(r.qty\_accepted, 0)) where id = r.grn\_line\_id;  
update inv.lots set unit\_landed\_cost\_minor = round((r.goods + r.added)::numeric / nullif(r.qty\_accepted, 0)) where grn\_line\_id = r.grn\_line\_id;  
\-- Simplified average update; a nightly costing job re-derives averages from the ledger as a control.  
insert into inv.item\_cost\_history(item\_id, effective\_at, avg\_cost\_minor, qty\_after, trigger\_type, trigger\_id)  
select r.item\_id, now(), round((h.avg\_cost\_minor \* h.qty\_after + r.added) / nullif(h.qty\_after, 0)), h.qty\_after, 'landed\_cost', p\_run  
from inv.item\_cost\_history h where h.item\_id = r.item\_id order by h.effective\_at desc limit 1;  
end loop;  
update proc.landed\_cost\_runs set status = 'posted', posted\_by = p\_user, posted\_at = now(),  
total\_allocated\_minor = (select coalesce(sum(amount\_minor), 0) from proc.landed\_cost\_allocations where run\_id = p\_run) where id = p\_run;  
insert into core.outbox\_events(topic, payload) values ('landed\_cost.posted', jsonb\_build\_object('run\_id', p\_run));  
end $$;

### Unit finalisation

create or replace function prod.finalise\_unit(p\_unit uuid, p\_inspection uuid, p\_user uuid) returns text language plpgsql security definer set search\_path = '' as $$  
declare u prod.units%rowtype; insp prod.qc\_inspections%rowtype; v\_serial text; v\_mat bigint; v\_lab bigint; v\_loc uuid;  
begin  
select \* into u from prod.units where id = p\_unit for update;  
if u.status <> 'qc\_hold' then raise exception 'UNIT\_NOT\_IN\_QC\_HOLD' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
select \* into insp from prod.qc\_inspections where id = p\_inspection and unit\_id = p\_unit;  
if not found or insp.result <> 'pass' then raise exception 'QC\_NOT\_PASSED' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
if exists (select 1 from unnest(array\['post', 'burn\_in'\]) rt(tt)  
where not exists (select 1 from prod.test\_runs t where t.unit\_id = p\_unit and t.test\_type = rt.tt and t.result = 'pass')) then  
raise exception 'TESTS\_INCOMPLETE' using errcode = 'P0001';  
end if;  
select coalesce(sum(round(uc.qty \* uc.unit\_cost\_minor)), 0) into v\_mat from prod.unit\_components uc where uc.unit\_id = p\_unit and uc.removed\_at is null;  
select coalesce(round(u.labour\_minutes\_total \* (select (s.value ->> 'labour\_rate\_per\_minute\_minor')::numeric from core.settings s where s.key = 'costing')), 0) into v\_lab;  
v\_serial := core.next\_doc\_no('UPSA-LAP');  
select id into v\_loc from core.locations where kind = 'warehouse' and active order by code limit 1;  
update prod.units set serial\_no = v\_serial, status = 'in\_stock', location\_id = v\_loc, qc\_passed\_at = now(),  
cost\_materials\_minor = v\_mat, cost\_labour\_minor = v\_lab, cost\_total\_minor = v\_mat + v\_lab where id = p\_unit;  
insert into inv.stock\_ledger(item\_id, location\_id, unit\_id, movement\_type, qty, unit\_cost\_minor, ref\_type, ref\_id, created\_by)  
values (u.item\_id, v\_loc, p\_unit, 'assembly\_output', 1, v\_mat + v\_lab, 'unit', p\_unit, p\_user);  
insert into core.outbox\_events(topic, payload) values ('unit.finalised', jsonb\_build\_object('unit\_id', p\_unit, 'serial', v\_serial));  
return v\_serial;  
end $$;

### Period lock and balanced journals

create or replace function fin.assert\_period\_open() returns trigger language plpgsql as $$  
declare p fin.fiscal\_periods%rowtype;  
begin  
select \* into p from fin.fiscal\_periods where id = new.period\_id;  
if p.status = 'closed' then raise exception 'PERIOD\_CLOSED' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
if new.entry\_date < p.starts\_on or new.entry\_date > p.ends\_on then raise exception 'DATE\_OUTSIDE\_PERIOD' using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
return new;  
end $$;  
create trigger trg\_journal\_entries\_period before insert on fin.journal\_entries for each row execute function fin.assert\_period\_open();  
  
\-- Every journal entry must balance (checked at commit).  
create or replace function fin.assert\_entry\_balanced() returns trigger language plpgsql as $$  
declare d bigint; c bigint;  
begin  
select coalesce(sum(debit\_minor), 0), coalesce(sum(credit\_minor), 0) into d, c from fin.journal\_lines where entry\_id = new.entry\_id;  
if d <> c then raise exception 'ENTRY\_UNBALANCED: debit % credit %', d, c using errcode = 'P0001'; end if;  
return null;  
end $$;  
create constraint trigger trg\_journal\_balanced after insert on fin.journal\_lines deferrable initially deferred for each row execute function fin.assert\_entry\_balanced();

8\. Security model
==================

*   **Writes:** browser roles have no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE rights anywhere. All writes use the API (service role) and the functions above.
*   **Reads:** RLS is enabled on every table. Each domain schema has a read policy based on JWT scopes; core tables have specific policies (own profile, own notifications, approvals for requesters and approvers, audit log only for audit.read).
*   **Technicians:** prod.units and prod.unit\_steps also allow rows where the user is the builder or assigned technician, so a technician’s own work is always visible.
*   **Sensitive columns:** bank\_details\_enc, new\_details\_enc, key\_enc, details\_enc, secret\_hash are excluded from column grants to authenticated.
*   **Views** use security\_invoker so RLS of the caller applies.
*   **Tables with no policy** (doc\_sequences, outbox\_events, idempotency\_keys, api\_clients) are reachable only by the service role.
*   **Audit:** audit rows never contain encrypted columns; before and after images are stored for business tables only.

| Finance & Service | catalog.read, supplier.bank.approve, landedcost.post, rma.write, inventory.read, orders.read, invoices.write, payments.write, expenses.submit, budgets.write, gl.read, gl.post\_manual, gl.close\_period, warranty.read, service.write, service.work, reports.read |
| Assembly Technician | catalog.read, inventory.read, production.work, tests.record, licence.view, expenses.submit, warranty.read, service.work |
| QC Inspector | catalog.read, inventory.read, count.run, tests.record, qc.inspect, rma.write, expenses.submit, warranty.read, service.work, reports.read |

These match the TDD permission matrix. Scope names are constants in packages/types; the database stores them as text so adding a scope needs no migration.

9\. Performance, partitioning and retention
===========================================

*   **Partitioning:** inv.stock\_ledger and core.audit\_log are range-partitioned by month with a default partition; 13 months are created at install and pg\_cron creates more.
*   **Indexes:** every foreign key has an index unless it leads a unique constraint; list filters have composite indexes (see table rules); BRIN on ledger time; GIN trigram and full-text indexes on item and supplier search.
*   **On-hand without counters:** month-end rows in inv.stock\_snapshots bound the scan; balances are views over snapshot plus ledger.
*   **Reports:** heavy aggregates run as background jobs against materialised views or a read replica when volume demands; none are created in v1.
*   **Connection use:** transaction pooling for the API; direct connections for migrations and the job runner.
*   **Retention:** audit and ledger partitions older than the retention period (default 10 years, to be confirmed) are detached and archived to storage; attachments follow their parent’s retention.
*   **Size estimate:** at a few hundred units a month the ledger grows by roughly 5,000 rows a day; ten years remain under a few hundred million rows total across partitions, well within a single Postgres instance.

11\. Import wizard templates
============================

Each template is an Excel or CSV sheet with a header row. The wizard validates every row, reports errors with reasons, and commits all or nothing; a committed batch can be rolled back until its rows are referenced.

| **Template** | **Columns (required in bold)** |
| --- | --- |
| Items | **sku**, **name**, **kind**, category, brand, family, uom, tracking, hs\_code, weight\_kg, warranty\_months, list\_price, barcode, reorder\_min, reorder\_qty, specs (key=value pairs) |
| Suppliers | **name**, **kind**, country, currency, payment\_terms, lead\_time\_days, contact\_name, email, phone, tin |
| Customer accounts | **name**, **kind**, department\_code, contact\_name, contact\_phone, contact\_email, cost\_centre, credit\_limit |
| BOMs | **finished\_sku**, **version**, **component\_sku**, **qty**, scrap\_pct, alt\_group, is\_optional, labour\_minutes |
| Opening stock | **sku**, **location\_code**, **qty**, **unit\_cost**, lot\_no, serial\_no (one row per serial), as\_of\_date |

Opening stock posts ledger rows of type opening and, for serial-tracked items, creates component\_serials; a supervised stock count follows.

12\. Migration plan
===================

| **Order** | **File** | **Contents** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 001 | 001\_extensions\_helpers.sql | Extensions, schemas, generic functions |
| 002 | 002\_core.sql | Core tables, auth hook, RLS helpers |
| 003 | 003\_catalog.sql | Catalogue and BOM |
| 004 | 004\_proc.sql | Procurement and imports |
| 005 | 005\_inv.sql | Ledger, lots, serials, counts |
| 006 | 006\_prod.sql | Production and QC |
| 007 | 007\_sales\_fin\_svc.sql | Sales, finance, service |
| 008 | 008\_foreign\_keys.sql | All foreign keys |
| 009 | 009\_indexes\_triggers.sql | Indexes, audit, doc numbers, append-only |
| 010 | 010\_functions\_views.sql | Domain functions and views |
| 011 | 011\_rls\_grants.sql | Policies and grants |
| 012 | 012\_seed.sql | Seed data |

*   Migrations are forward-only; changes follow expand then contract; destructive steps need a second reviewer.
*   Drizzle schema files in packages/database are generated from the live schema (drizzle-kit pull), never hand-edited.
*   Preview environments run Supabase branches seeded with fixture data of ten times the expected volume.

13\. Validation and test plan
=============================

13.1 Done during authoring
--------------------------

*   Whole script parsed (1,293 statements) and executed without error on PostgreSQL with stubs for Supabase auth.
*   Verified: append-only rejection on the ledger, unbalanced journal rejection at commit, closed-period rejection, document numbering, access-token hook output, landed-cost allocation with exact sums.

13.2 pgTAP suite to write in Phase 1
------------------------------------

1.  Every table has RLS enabled and no write policies for authenticated.
2.  For each role template, the expected tables are readable and others return zero rows.
3.  Suspended users receive no scopes from the hook.
4.  Encrypted columns are not selectable by authenticated.
5.  Ledger, audit, cost history and timelines reject UPDATE and DELETE.
6.  Two concurrent reservations of the same unit: one succeeds, one raises.
7.  Receipt posting is idempotent: a second call writes no rows.
8.  Landed-cost run: allocations sum to each charge for value, weight, volume and quantity bases, including rounding edge cases.
9.  Reversal of a posted run restores the prior unit cost.
10.  finalise\_unit fails without passing tests or QC, and fails when the inspector built the unit.
11.  Dispatch of a unit not in stock or reserved elsewhere fails.
12.  Journal entry per source and event is unique; unbalanced entries fail; closed periods reject.
13.  Approval requester cannot decide their own request.
14.  Partitions exist for the next 12 months; inserts outside fall to the default partition and raise an alert.
15.  v\_stock\_available equals ledger sum minus active reservations on a seeded dataset.
16.  prod.v\_unit\_cost live cost equals frozen cost for finalised units without replacements.
